title: The Boy King and His Regents

title_i18n.en: The Boy King and His Regents

subtitle: An eleven-year-old ascends a throne of iron frontiers and hungry neighbours.
region: Ajmer, Delhi, Bundelkhand and the Gahadavala frontier
moral: A crown given to a child is a test of the men around it before it is a test of the child.

sources.note: Prithviraj's own record that he 'laid waste Jejakabhukti' (the Chandella Bundelkhand).
Records the defeat of the Bhadanakas and a peace treaty with Bhima II of Gujarat.

sources.citation: Cynthia Talbot, The Last Hindu Emperor (2015), pp. 38-40; Dasharatha Sharma, Early Chauhan Dynasties (1959), pp. 72-74

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle hero wide against the ramparts of Ajmer at sunset

dialogue.text: In 1177, boy-king Prithviraj Chauhan takes Ajmer’s throne at eleven—while grown men decide whether he will be shield, pawn, or weapon.

panels.shot: slow push-in on a coronation scene inside Ajmer’s palace hall

dialogue.text: The Madanpur inscription dates his reign from Vikrama 1234. Ajmer’s drums thunder, but the new Chahamana ruler is still a child.

panels.shot: medium shot over the boy’s shoulder towards his mother and minister

dialogue.text: For some years, power rests in other hands. His mother Karpuradevi and the seasoned minister Kadambavasa rule in his name, holding the realm together.

panels.shot: tight close-up on Prithviraj’s young face watching from behind a curtain

dialogue.text: The boy listens more than he speaks. Around him, Rajasthan’s Rajput clans watch Ajmer’s court, weighing whether the child’s reign means weakness.

panels.shot: map-table overhead shot showing rival regions marked by figurines

dialogue.text: To the east lies Gahadavala Kannauj, to the south Chandella Jejakabhukti, to the west Gujarat. Each power grows. Ajmer cannot stand still.

panels.shot: dramatic interior wide as a messenger bursts into council

dialogue.text: Sometime around 1180, one challenge can no longer be ignored: a kinsman, Nagarjuna, has risen in revolt at Gudapura, testing the young king’s authority.

panels.shot: low-angle mounted wide shot of Prithviraj leading a column out of Ajmer

dialogue.text: “If I cannot command my own blood, I command nothing.”

panels.shot: mid-shot battlefield tableau with two camps facing off near a fort

dialogue.text: Chroniclers remember that Nagarjuna’s revolt is crushed. The boy who rode out under regents returns having shown he can lead war himself.

panels.shot: solemn interior shot of an audience hall, Prithviraj now central and commanding

dialogue.text: After Gudapura, power tilts. By around 1180, Prithviraj has taken personal control. The regency fades; the boy-king becomes the decision-maker.

panels.shot: dynamic travel montage shot of riders crossing varied terrain

dialogue.text: His first outward test lies to the east. The Bhadanakas, a lesser power near Delhi, challenge his expansion. Jain records later note their defeat.

panels.shot: wide angled shot of a tense standoff near a small fortified town

dialogue.text: There is no epic poem for this fight, only terse lines in chronicles: Prithviraj defeats the Bhadanakas, tightening his grip around Delhi’s hinterland.

panels.shot: overhead shot on a map with Prithviraj’s token edging towards Jejakabhukti

dialogue.text: With Bhadanaka resistance broken, his gaze turns to Chandella lands. Between Ajmer and Kannauj, Bundelkhand sits like a wedge of stone.

panels.shot: long shot of the column approaching rocky Bundelkhand terrain at dawn

dialogue.text: Talbot’s study and the Madanpur inscription agree: Prithviraj pushes into Jejakabhukti, not to rule it, but to strike and withdraw.

panels.shot: dramatic wide shot of Mahoba’s fort under siege-like pressure without gore

dialogue.text: The Madanpur inscription of 1182–83 boasts that he “laid waste Jejakabhukti.” It is the language of a raid, not of settled rule.

panels.shot: mid-shot of Prithviraj looking back from horseback as the city smoulders behind

dialogue.text: Paramardi, the Chandella king, survives and rules for years. The Chahamana raid wounds, but does not break, the Bundelkhand throne.

panels.shot: contrast shot of wandering bards singing in a village square

dialogue.text: Later legend fills this campaign with Alha, Udal, and endless duels. The records are quieter: they speak of a harsh raid, not of a conquered realm.

panels.shot: palace audience shot with a Gujarati envoy before Prithviraj

dialogue.text: Beyond the east, another frontier needs calm. Jain chronicles record a treaty with Gujarat’s Bhima II, balancing war on one side with peace on another.

panels.shot: medium shot of Prithviraj at a balcony, gazing toward the Ganga plains

dialogue.text: By his early twenties, he has crushed a cousin, beaten the Bhadanakas, raided Bundelkhand, and secured Gujarat. Ahead looms Kannauj and the Gahadavala power.

panels.shot: slow push-in close-up on Prithviraj’s contemplative profile at twilight

dialogue.text: His youth’s story is not of romance but of regents, rebels and raids. It asks: when a crown falls on a child’s head, whose choices truly shape the kingdom’s path?
